plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers that open in the cool season. It is widely grown in gardens and parks and has thousands of cultivars with single, semi-double, and fully double blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (December to March in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and eastern China; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant that gives us tea, and camellia seed oil has been used for centuries in East Asia for cooking and hair care.

plants.name: Hamamelis mollis
plants.description: A deciduous large shrub or small tree that flowers on bare branches in the depths of winter. Its spidery, ribbon-like petals curl up in freezing weather and unfurl again when it warms, and the blooms give off a sweet spicy fragrance.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Native to central and eastern China; grown in temperate gardens across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Witch hazel flowers can curl their petals tightly to protect themselves from frost and then reopen, and extracts from related species are used in astringent skin products.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial with strap-like leaves and tall stems topped with rounded clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere it is at its peak in midsummer and is a common sight in gardens, roadsides, and coastal areas.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February)
plants.location: Native to South Africa; widely planted and naturalized in Australia, New Zealand, and parts of South America
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, Agapanthus is not a true lily; its name comes from the Greek words for 'love' and 'flower'.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that blooms on bare branches in the coldest part of the year, often when snow is still on the ground. Its fragrant five-petaled blossoms are among the earliest signs that spring is coming in East Asia.
plants.location: Native to southern China; cultivated across Japan, Korea, and China, as well as in botanical gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: In East Asian culture the plum blossom symbolizes perseverance and hope, and it is one of the 'Three Friends of Winter' along with pine and bamboo.
